newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to shut down seven coal mines in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Poland to shut down seven coal mines in 1997.

text.p: Poland will shut down seven of its 57 state-owned coal mines in 1997 and cut 17,000 jobs as part of the ailing sector's restructuring scheme, a deputy economy minister said on Monday.

"Mining will be stopped in three pits and...four mines in which excavation was earlier halted would be completely liquidated," Jerzy Markowski said after a session of the government's economic council (KERM).

He told a news briefing that 240,000 workers were employed by the coal industry. Their number would be reduced by about 17,000 but there would be no collective layoffs in the politically sensitive sector.
"People will go on early retirements and no new workers will be hired," he said.
Coal output would decline to about 125 million tonnes in 1997 from more than 130,000 tonnes last year. About 27 million tonnes will be exported, Markowski said.
The government plan envisages that the mining sector, burdened with debts exceeding nine billion zlotys, would cut employment to 170,000 in 2000 and reduce the number of pits to 46.
As part of the revival programme, the government is considering a plan to freeze all mines' liabilities to the treasury until 2000.
Markowski said losses in the industry, burdened with high costs and low coal prices, was likely to total 800 million zlotys in 1997.
